response.markdown_report:
The best initial experiment remains **uniform-smoothed self-adversarial pairwise training with separately tested absolute-event recency weighting**, preserving corrected GRU4Rec. Recency is conditional on verifying the supplied sampler’s effective exposure.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Electronics has the weakest sampled discrimination: 9.7% wrong-order comparisons and a 0.0265 lower-decile margin. This motivates ranking experiments, without establishing validation performance. (2) Mapped embedding similarities near 0.5 imply mean cosine similarities near zero; collapse regularization lacks supporting evidence. (3) Users distinguish specific current intent from broad historical relevance. Competitive supervision and recent-target emphasis target weak-match displacement and stale-interest revival, but cannot establish compatibility or satisfied needs.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [MTAM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.08598) motivates temporal retention, with greater integration cost. (2) [RotatE](https://github.com/DeepGraphLearning/KnowledgeGraphEmbedding/blob/master/codes/model.py) establishes detached self-adversarial weighting, although its losses differ. (3) [BPR-max](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf) and [PSL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.00163) use distinct objectives; their analyses do not transfer to this heuristic. (4) [Ask the GRU](https://ciir-publications.cs.umass.edu/getpdf.php?id=1255) motivates jointly learned text features, subject to architectural and initialization differences.

**Framework and candidate directions.** Supervision controls historical target exposure; ranking controls candidate competition; representation controls expressible similarities. Diagnose sampler exposure before adding temporal complexity.

Scores use O=originality, P=potential, U=user alignment, M=model alignment, D=implementation difficulty; higher D means harder. Scores assess hypotheses, not demonstrated gains.

| Idea | O/P/U/M/D | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Smoothed competitive loss plus conditional event recency | 3/6/7/8/5 | Tests two reported user failures and weak sampled separation without inference changes | Established ingredients; exposure analysis and controlled sampling increase implementation effort |
| Joint time-conditioned GRU retention | 5/7/8/6/7 | Represents changing intent inside recurrent state | Requires consistently available timestamps and careful gate diagnosis |
| Joint title-token item residuals | 4/7/7/6/6 | Could support sparse, identifiable media matches | Shared words may reinforce broad-similarity shortcuts |

**Selected algorithm.** Average pairwise logistic losses with 0.75 uniform mass and 0.25 detached negative-score softmax mass. Sample up to 16 distinct eligible negatives: uniqueness makes the coefficient bound apply per item within a position. This bounds score-gradient contributions, not parameter gradients or false-negative harm. Add mild original-event recency only after measuring exposure under actual crops; old-only and singleton crops may receive negligible or zero change.

This explicitly targets stale-interest revival and weakly connected candidates displacing specific matches; Electronics’ sampled ordering errors are the model-facing target. Neither hypothesis guarantees immediate usefulness.

Compare baseline, matched control, loss-only, recency-only and combined alternatives only as budget permits; never fuse them. Select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10. Log all evaluated checkpoints to expose selection bias. Conditional paired intervals require host-provided hit indicators. Sampled gains need not transfer to full-catalog ranking ([Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). Preserve four routes, seeds, limits, diagnostic contracts and matching predictor serialization. Track qualitative rejection reasons separately; claim no improvement before measurement.

idea.description: Keep the supplied corrected GRU4Rec backbone and test uniform-smoothed, detached self-adversarial pairwise logistic supervision, with a separately controlled mild absolute-event recency arm. Train and deploy exactly one independent checkpoint per category. Use distinct negative items within each position so the stated allocation bound applies per item there.
idea.motivation: The combined hypothesis targets two observed user-facing failures: stale interests resurfacing and weakly connected recommendations displacing specific recent-intent matches. Recency changes target emphasis; competitive allocation redirects a limited share of supervision toward difficult alternatives while preserving uniform coverage. Electronics’ 9.7% sampled wrong-order rate, 14.82% small-margin rate and 0.0265 tenth-percentile margin motivate the model-facing target. These are sampled ordering errors, not evidence that sampled negatives are confirmed dislikes. Neither component provides compatibility, ownership-satisfaction, quantity, mood or immediate-purpose labels. The architecture alternatives remain plausible later directions, but progress is 0%, so controlled training changes receive priority.
idea.implementation_notes:
Scope and integration: the actual supplied baseline source is absent from this prompt. This is an integration component, not a complete replacement train.py, and no execution or improvement is claimed. Preserve the corrected GRU architecture, optimizer, initialization, score transformation, recurrent reset/carry policy, dropout, batch size, history length and checkpoint cadence initially. Record their resolved values during host integration. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch. Resolve the environment default SASREC_EPOCHS=200 while enforcing the 200-epoch cap. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; save all artifacts beneath the trial directory. Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl routing, fixed splits, single-GPU execution and the unchanged evaluator. Use no external weights, extra datasets, hidden test files or other-trial checkpoints.

Comparison order and budget: prespecify baseline, matched mean-pairwise control, competitive-loss-only, recency-only and combined comparisons, retaining only those affordable within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Diagnostics, debugging and failed trials count. Reuse the supplied baseline result only when its protocol and resolved settings are documented; do not reuse another trial’s trained checkpoint. The matched control uses competitive_mass=0 and uniform temporal weights with the same negatives and reduction as the proposed loss. If supplied baseline sampling, objective or reduction differs, disclose the matched control as a separate intervention. A baseline-objective arm consuming the same negatives is useful only when doing so preserves a clearly specified objective. Keep initialization, windows, negative tensors, optimizer, update budget, validation cadence and checkpoint tie-breaking identical across controlled arms. Equal updates do not imply equal runtime. Generate training draws using a dedicated seed-42 sampler stream, separate from dropout/model randomness; replay draws or deterministically derive them from update indices. Alternative arms are independently evaluated experiments and must never be fused, averaged or deployed together.

Negative sampling: for each valid training position, sample K_u=min(16, number_of_eligible_items) distinct IDs uniformly without replacement from real catalog IDs excluding padding, the target and the user’s complete observed training history. Use only training interactions for exclusions; never consult validation/test positives. Rejection sampling with both history-membership checks and a local selected-ID set is acceptable; use explicit eligible-set construction when rejection becomes inefficient. When fewer than 16 eligible items exist, use all of them and mask unused columns before normalization. Skip positions with no eligible items and record their count. Distinct sampling changes the earlier with-replacement proposal and must be applied to all matched controls. It avoids duplicate-column concentration but does not detect false negatives. Across different positions, the same item can still accumulate supervision. Log eligible counts, actual unique counts and skipped positions.

Objective definition: let alpha=0.25, temperature=2, and p_j=softmax(s_neg/temperature)_j over eligible distinct items. Define w_j=(1-alpha)/K_u+alpha*stopgrad(p_j), and L_position=sum_j w_j*softplus(s_neg_j-s_pos). Detach the competitive allocation intentionally. The negative score derivative is w_j*sigmoid(s_neg_j-s_pos), and the positive derivative is the negative sum of these terms. Without detachment, additional derivatives through the allocation change the update. Each item’s coefficient within a position is at most alpha+(1-alpha)/K_u, but parameter gradients also depend on score Jacobians. Do not describe this as verified noise robustness. It is uniform-smoothed self-adversarial weighted BPR, related to RotatE’s allocation mechanism; RotatE uses different pointwise logistic losses. It is neither BPR-max nor PSL. BPR-max puts a negative logarithm outside a weighted probability sum and differentiates its weights; PSL reshapes a different aggregate through activation functions. Their theoretical guarantees do not transfer. Do not add logQ correction or a negative-score penalty to this initial pairwise experiment.

Temporal weighting: for target original zero-based training index k in full user history length T, use age=T-1-k and a(k)=0.5+0.5*exp(-age/10). Carry original indices through cropping in a separate training side channel. Weights are 1 at age zero, about 0.684 at age 10 and 0.525 at age 30, tending to 0.5. Normalize weighted position losses within each sampled window, then average nonempty windows. Apply exactly this reduction to the uniform control. Describe it as per-window normalization, not equal-user weighting or exposure normalization. Singleton windows are unchanged, and old-only windows approach uniform weighting. Original target age must not be replaced with crop-relative age. If original indices cannot be supplied reliably, disable the temporal arm.

Sampler exposure prerequisite: for the actual crop C and retained valid targets S(C), effective target mass is E_C[1{k in S(C)}*a(k)/sum_{j in S(C)}a(j)]. Uniform-control mass is E_C[1{k in S(C)}/|S(C)|]. These generally cannot be reduced to inclusion probability times a globally normalized age weight. Analyze the exact supplied sampler by enumeration where feasible, otherwise Monte Carlo with a separate analysis RNG and identical crops for both weighting conditions. Accumulate normalized coefficients for each original event; report inclusion frequency separately from effective mass. Plot or tabulate mass and weighted/uniform mass ratios by absolute age, history length and crop length, excluding padding and reporting counts. Targets absent from all crops remain unexposed. Confirm whether recent events actually receive additional mass before attributing behavior to recency. Report effective sample size (sum weights)^2/sum squared weights as a descriptive weight-concentration measure. These quantities measure supervision mass, not gradient magnitude or validation improvement. Do not add recency-based sampling simultaneously.

Diagnostics and interfaces: preserve family-specific sample_batch and ModelView, view.model as the actual trained nn.Module, item_emb, aligned B×L log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning measured metrics and metric_definitions, and callable diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), retaining measured values and definitions. Diagnostic batches remain (None, sequence, positive, negative), each tensor B×L. Original target indices and multiple optimization negatives belong to a separate training path. Keep diagnostic examples and negative draws fixed across arms where possible; valid diagnostic positions require nonzero sequence, positive and negative IDs. Preserve margin definitions and distinguish score-scale inflation from changes in wrong-order rates. Mapped embedding similarities near 0.5 do not establish collapse. Available data are public interaction histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps. Ratings, review text, category metadata, prices, stores and simulator traits remain unavailable; mark category breakdowns unavailable rather than interpreting empty lists as absence of errors.

Encoding and export: retain the supplied padding-invariant corrected GRU. Verify that valid states and candidate scores match individual unpadded executions in evaluation mode, including empty, singleton, mixed-length and reordered batches. For left-padded histories, final readout uses the maximum nonpadding position, never count-1. Preserve documented empty-history handling. No inference feature change is required by this objective. The predictor writer must nevertheless export the exact trained architecture, score transformation and configuration. Each category loads exactly one selected checkpoint. No independent transition/popularity predictor, mixture of fitted experts, checkpoint averaging or score fusion is permitted.

Validation and inference: use only pinned macro validation HR@10 with 200 users per category, 99 unique negatives and evaluation seed 42. Preserve the inherited selection rule and validation cadence, documenting their resolved values before comparisons rather than inventing an alternative schedule. Record every evaluated configuration/checkpoint and category-level HR. One changed hit changes category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. If the host provides paired per-user hit indicators, compute 10,000 paired bootstrap replicates by resampling 200 users within each category, using common resamples across arms and a separate analysis RNG seed 42; report category effects and the equally weighted macro difference with a 95% interval. A paired randomization test is optional for prespecified contrasts. Do not modify the evaluator or reconstruct indicators from aggregate scores. These intervals condition on trained seed-42 models and fixed candidates, omit training/candidate variability and do not correct adaptive winner selection. Account for multiplicity in prespecified comparisons where used, disclose all search effort and treat small gains as exploratory. Sampled metrics can reverse full-catalog model ordering; claim gains only for the pinned benchmark. Freeze selection before the host’s separate final held-out evaluation.

User-facing assessment and shortcuts: preserve native full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for the same twenty real training users, five per category. Track stale-interest objections, unrelated-purpose rejections and specific-current-intent endorsements separately from broad relevance. Keep compatibility, redundancy, quantity, deferred interest and unidentified content as separate observed judgments. Do not infer them from margins or HR. Recency may overemphasize transient behavior; competitive sampling may suppress relevant unseen items or reward popularity correlations. Examine observed rejection patterns and training-derived history-length/item-frequency strata with counts, without inventing new labels or replacing the selection metric. Joint text features remain deferred because shared words can reinforce the diagnosed broad-similarity shortcut.
idea.pseudocode:
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F


def bounded_competitive_loss(pos, neg, valid, negative_mask,
                             target_age=None,
                             competitive_mass=0.25,
                             temperature=2.0):
    """pos [B,L], neg [B,L,K], valid [B,L], negative_mask [B,L,K].
    Each position's eligible negative IDs must be distinct.
    target_age uses ORIGINAL training-event indices.
    Reduction: normalized windows, then mean over nonempty windows.
    """
    if neg.shape[-1] < 1 or temperature <= 0:
        raise ValueError('Require negative slots and positive temperature')
    if not 0 <= competitive_mass <= 1:
        raise ValueError('Invalid competitive mass')
    negative_mask = negative_mask.bool()
    active_position = valid.bool() & negative_mask.any(dim=-1)
    rows, cols = active_position.nonzero(as_tuple=True)
    if rows.numel() == 0:
        return pos[active_position].sum() * 0.0

    p = pos[rows, cols].float()
    n = neg[rows, cols].float()
    mask = negative_mask[rows, cols]
    count = mask.sum(-1, keepdim=True).float()
    allocation_logits = (n.detach() / temperature).masked_fill(
        ~mask, -torch.inf)
    competitive = F.softmax(allocation_logits, dim=-1)
    uniform = mask.float() / count
    allocation = ((1.0 - competitive_mass) * uniform
                  + competitive_mass * competitive)
    # Replace unused scores before arithmetic to avoid 0 * inf or NaN.
    safe_n = n.masked_fill(~mask, 0.0)
    pair_loss = F.softplus(safe_n - p[:, None]).masked_fill(~mask, 0.0)
    position_loss = (allocation * pair_loss).sum(-1)

    weight = torch.ones_like(p)
    if target_age is not None:
        age = target_age[rows, cols].float()
        if not torch.isfinite(age).all() or (age < 0).any():
            raise ValueError('Invalid original-event ages')
        weight = 0.5 + 0.5 * torch.exp(-age / 10.0)

    numerator = torch.zeros(pos.shape[0], device=p.device)
    denominator = torch.zeros_like(numerator)
    numerator.scatter_add_(0, rows, weight * position_loss)
    denominator.scatter_add_(0, rows, weight)
    active_window = denominator > 0
    return (numerator[active_window] / denominator[active_window]).mean()


# Integration with the supplied corrected baseline:
# 1. Record inherited configuration, sampler law and selection schedule.
# 2. Preserve seeds, four routes, fixed splits, GRU and optimizer.
# 3. Prespecify affordable controls and log all evaluated checkpoints.
# 4. Replay identical windows and distinct negative IDs across matched arms.
# 5. For each position, uniformly sample min(16, eligible_count) distinct
#    negatives excluding padding and complete known training history.
#    Mask unused slots; omit positions with no eligible negatives.
# 6. Retain original target indices through a separate training side channel.
# 7. Measure effective target exposure under the actual crop/reduction law:
#       uniform coefficient = 1 / retained_target_count
#       weighted coefficient = a(original_index) / sum_retained(a)
#    Aggregate by original event, age, history length and crop length.
# 8. Enable the temporal arm only with valid indices and measured exposure.
# 9. features = model.log2feats(sequence).
#    Score positive and K negative items with unchanged score transformations.
# 10. valid requires nonzero sequence/positive IDs and eligible negatives.
#     age = full_training_length[:, None] - 1 - original_target_index.
# 11. Matched control: competitive_mass=0, target_age=None.
#     Loss-only: competitive_mass=0.25, target_age=None.
#     Recency-only: competitive_mass=0, target_age=age.
#     Combined: competitive_mass=0.25, target_age=age.
# 12. Verify K=1 equality with ordinary pairwise logistic loss, masking,
#     sampler uniqueness/exclusions, singleton-weight cancellation,
#     finite gradients and the detached-allocation derivative formula.
# 13. Preserve BxL diagnostic batches, fixed diagnostic draws and definitions.
# 14. Select solely by unchanged host macro validation HR@10.
#     Conditional paired uncertainty requires host-provided hit indicators.
# 15. Export one chosen checkpoint/category and matching embedded predictor.
#     Final readout uses maximum nonpadding index; handle empty rows.
#     Never combine experimental arms or independent scores.

originality.positive: The constrained combination of smoothed self-adversarial pairwise supervision, unique-item allocation bounds and sampler-aware recency analysis creates a clear diagnosis-driven GRU4Rec experiment.
originality.negative: Detached self-adversarial weighting, pairwise logistic ranking and recency weighting are established. The method introduces no new model class and inherits neither PSL nor BPR-max theory.

future_potential.positive: Controlled comparisons can identify whether candidate competition or historical target exposure deserves further investment before temporal gates or jointly trained text features.
future_potential.negative: No validation gain is demonstrated. Mild recency may largely cancel within crops, and the method cannot directly model compatibility, satisfied needs or immediate purpose.

code_difficulty.positive: The loss is compact and preserves the GRU architecture, inference inputs and checkpoint structure.
code_difficulty.negative: Distinct eligible sampling, original-index tracking, exact sampler-exposure analysis, deterministic controls and predictor–diagnostic consistency require substantial baseline-specific integration.

related_work.title: MTAM (CIKM 2020)
contributions: Uses temporal gating in recurrent information processing to model evolving interests.
Motivates a later architecture-level experiment on hidden-state retention.
limitations: Does not establish gains under the pinned four-category evaluation.
Its additional memory mechanisms exceed the selected minimal training intervention.

related_work.title: RotatE: self-adversarial negative sampling implementation
contributions: Provides an established implementation of detached score-based negative allocation.
Clarifies that detaching allocation changes the update rather than merely numerical scaling.
limitations: Uses pointwise logistic losses for knowledge graph embeddings rather than this sequential pairwise objective.
Does not establish false-negative robustness or Amazon recommendation gains for the proposed mixture.

related_work.title: Recurrent Neural Networks with Top-k Gains for Session-based Recommendations
contributions: Introduces BPR-max as a negative logarithm of a softmax-weighted preference-probability sum.
Provides a directly relevant recurrent recommendation objective for a separately specified comparison.
limitations: BPR-max differs mathematically from detached weighted pairwise logistic loss.
Its sampling procedure and differentiated allocation must not be silently attributed to the proposed method.

related_work.title: PSL (NeurIPS 2024)
contributions: Examines aggressive negative influence and develops alternative activation-based pairwise formulations.
Motivates studying the gradient influence of uncertain high-scoring negatives.
limitations: Uniform-smoothed self-adversarial weighting is not the published PSL objective.
PSL’s analysis does not establish robustness of the proposed heuristic, and exposure remains unobserved.

related_work.title: Ask the GRU (2016)
contributions: Provides a precedent for jointly optimized text representations with item-specific residual embeddings.
Motivates a future single-network title/description representation experiment.
limitations: Its GRU processes document text rather than interaction histories.
Its externally pretrained word embeddings cannot be imported under the current constraints.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can disagree with full-catalog evaluation, including model ordering.
Supports interpreting results specifically within the pinned 100-candidate benchmark.
limitations: Does not justify changing the host evaluator.
Narrower uncertainty intervals do not remove candidate-sampling bias.

related_work.title: Statistical Inference at Scale: Evaluating Recommendation Systems
contributions: Supports paired statistical inference for recommendation comparisons.
Motivates resampling user pairs while retaining category stratification.
limitations: Paired analysis requires per-user outcomes that the host may not expose.
Fixed-model, fixed-candidate intervals omit training variability and adaptive selection effects.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains optimistic bias introduced by repeated model and hyperparameter selection.
Motivates logging all evaluated configurations and freezing selection before independent final evaluation.
limitations: Winner-only confidence intervals do not correct adaptive validation reuse.
The study does not supply an additional permitted validation split or alter this task’s fixed protocol.
